newsitem.title: UK: Pay TV deals could yield $1.0 bln revenues to BBC.
newsitem.headline: Pay TV deals could yield $1.0 bln revenues to BBC.

text.p: The BBC could get revenues of almost $1.0 billion from two joint ventures to provide multi-channel pay-television with UK satellite cable broadcaster Flextech Plc in Britain and one with its parent in North America.

Adam Singer, the president and chief operating officer of Flextech's U.S. parent Tele-Communications International Inc, told a news conference he expected to see "close to $1.0 billion coming back to the BBC over the next three or four years".
Singer was speaking after Flextech and BBC Worldwide Ltd, the commercial arm of the BBC, unveiled details of two planned joint ventures to develop and launch new subscription channels in Britian.

Flextech, along with the backing of its U.S. parent, is providing the funding and marketing expertise for the ventures and the BBC is contributing its diverse archive, scheduling and production skills.
"Outside the UK, the BBC is probably the last, great, under-utilised English language library in the world," Singer said.
